name: The Chudobín Pine

location.address: Rocky outcrop on the left (Chudobín) bank of the Vír reservoir, near the former village of Chudobín, Dalečín municipality, Žďár nad Sázavou District, Vysočina Region

access: View-only. The tree stands on a rocky promontory inside the reservoir's protected water-source buffer zone and cannot be approached (root damage risk on exposed rock). It is viewed from a signed viewpoint on the public path along the reservoir's right bank, facing across the water. Free.
transport: Rural, no public transport nearby; reached on foot along the marked path on the right bank of the Vír reservoir, Vysočina Region. Nearest town is Vír.
verify_notes: Solitary Scots pine on a rock outcrop above the former Hamr weir, submerged when the Vír reservoir was built in 1957; the tree survived on what became an island/promontory. Won the Czech 'Strom roku' (Tree of the Year) 2019 public vote (16,000+ voters, its 18th edition), then European Tree of the Year 2020 with 47,226 votes, the first Czech tree to win. Nominated by Milan Peňáz, a former resident of the flooded village. Age is disputed: a 2019 dendrological assessment by doc. Ing. L. Úradníček (Mendel University Faculty of Forestry) put it at 300-350 years; a later Povodí Moravy (river authority) assessment says it could be 500+ years but the trunk has an internal cavity that prevents precise ring-count dating, so state both loosely rather than pick a winner. Distinctive S-shaped trunk from wind and rock-face growth; roots partly exposed on bare rock, submerged at high reservoir levels and standing over 20m above the waterline at low levels. Condition rated excellent/healthy in multiple assessments (2019 and later), though the 2019 Wikipedia-cited source also notes reduced vitality signs from long-term drought and water-level fluctuation; treat as a healthy but stressed veteran rather than pristine. PMO source gives trunk circumference 188cm (~60cm diameter) and height 13m. This qualifies for the single-famous-tree exception (2026-08-31): European Tree of the Year winners draw dedicated visits and this is a genuinely singular destination with nothing else nearby to cluster it with. Access is honestly view-only; pin marks the tree's own known coordinate (from cs.wikipedia infobox) rather than the viewpoint itself, whose exact coordinate was not found this pass, hence approximate precision.

name: The Guardian Oak of Víska

location.address: Southern edge of the Víska settlement, beside the road and footbridge over the Smědá river, Višňová municipality, Liberec District, Liberec Region

access: Free, on a public road at the edge of the village, beside the bridge over the Smědá. An information board and a seating area for visitors stand beneath it.
transport: No rail; reached by local bus to Višňová/Víska (Liberec District) or by car, then a short walk to the village's southern edge.
verify_notes: Known locally as 'Dub ochránce' (the Guardian Oak). During catastrophic flash flooding on the Smědá on 7 August 2010, the oak's trunk caught and held back a mass of floating trees and debris carried by the flood, sparing houses downstream; local accounts credit it with protecting a couple and their dog as well. Won the Czech 'Strom roku' (Tree of the Year) public vote in 2013, then placed fifth in the European Tree of the Year competition the following year (2014). Arborists carried out a canopy health prune in September 2014. Two independent sources agree on the story and the 2013/2014 award; only turistika.cz gives the physical measurements (455cm girth, 20m height) and only Czech Wikipedia gives the approximate age (150 years, stated as of the article, not pinned to a specific year). Coordinates differ slightly between sources (turistika.cz's page gives 50.944, 15.028, roughly 600m from this lead's original 50.938917, 15.02725); used turistika's more specific 'south edge of Víska by the bridge' description and its coordinate, hence approximate precision rather than confirmed. This qualifies for the single-famous-tree exception (2026-08-31): a tree with a genuine flood-heroism story, a national award and international placing, standing on its own at a village edge with nothing to cluster it with.

name: The Pear Tree in the Middle of the Field

location.address: In an open field north above the village of Mrákotín, opposite a farmstead, near the road to Malinné, Chrudim District, Pardubice Region

access: Free. Stands alone in a working arable field beside the road to Malinné; no formal marked trail found, but a tourism source describes reaching it 'without problems' along the field edge even when the surrounding field is sown with crop. Informal field-edge access rather than a paved path.
transport: Rural, no public transport nearby; reached by car or on foot from Mrákotín village, Chrudim District.
verify_notes: A solitary common pear standing in open farmland, its lopsided crown shaped by strong prevailing west winds and its exposed, treeless position; the subject of the well-known Czech folk song 'Stojí hruška v širém poli' ('A pear tree stands in the open field'). Officially protected as a 'památný strom' since 11 April 1996 (AOPK CR register no. 101575/8375). Estimated age 110 years, which the sources note is old for a pear (the species can live to roughly 200). Survived collectivisation, field consolidation (scelování poli), land drainage works and inexpert pruning over that time. Won the Czech 'Strom roku' (Tree of the Year) 2023 public vote with 6,433 votes and went on to the European Tree of the Year competition the same year. This qualifies for the single-famous-tree exception (2026-08-31): a national Tree of the Year winner with its own folk song and no other trees to cluster it with; would draw a dedicated visit on its own merits.
